news.title: Friendship World Cup: Martinje 2026 brings together sports legends, Ivica Šurjak is the wine godfather of the Kutjevo winery
news.lede: Martinje 2026 in Ulcinj brought together numerous sports legends of the former Yugoslavia, and the famous football player Ivica Šurjak was declared the wine godfather of the Kutjevo winery, reports Media Biro. The celebration of wine, friendship and togetherness this year gained special significance through its connection with the fifth, jubilee Friendship World Cup. This year's Martinje once again showed that wine can be much more than tradition and customs, and that it is an occasion for people to meet who are connected by sport, shared memories and sincere friendship. The centerpiece of the celebration was the announcement of a new wine godfather.

news.title: From U-17 World Cup to Brazil: Indian football keeps finding hope, but how long does it last?
news.lede: In October 2017, when I was 16, I walked into Salt Lake Stadium believing I was getting a glimpse of Indian football's future. The stadium had been transformed for the FIFA Under-17 World Cup, the stands were buzzing, and I was watching Brazil, England and Spain play on a stage that seemed a world away from the football infrastructure I had grown up seeing in India.Almost nine years later, I returned to the same ground, this time carrying a laptop and a journalist's notebook.The excitement of watching world-class football in my hometown was still there, but so did a question I had not thought of asking as a teenager. What happens after the big teams leave? October 28, 2017, remains a special day in my football memories.

news.title: Cruel ‘reality check’ key for Tillies stars to elevate World Cup auditions
news.lede: A cruel “reality check” from Germany could be the awakening the Matildas need heading into the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, according to Craig Foster. Joe Montemurro needed little time to see the weaknesses in his team’s tactics, as Australia’s beloved national team suffered a 4-2 loss to Germany on Saturday. Germany celebrate after their fourth goal against the Matildas. Germany needed half an hour to find the back of the net twice, with countless chances presented before those two goals also.

news.title: Four mega stadiums under construction now from £28bn beast to 115,000 seater World Cup venue
news.lede: Sports fans across the globe will soon get to grace a number of huge new stadiums with some ambitious plans already in the works. As clubs and countries vie for prestige on the international stage, a number of exciting stadium projects are aiming to bring in even more fans and greater revenues to their owners. The construction of new grounds can result from sports or clubs gaining immense popularity, or from nations seeking to offer a contemporary stadium design for an upcoming competition or tournament. That is certainly the case for some of the most exciting projects under construction at the moment, with some having already broken ground and hoping for grand openings in the next few years.

news.title: Football: Soccer-US will learn from bruising friendly defeat by Spain, says Hayes
news.lede: Oct 10 (Reuters) - US women's coach Emma ⁠Hayes shook off a dismal 2-0 defeat on Saturday in the first of ⁠two friendlies against Spain, with the Americans building towards next month's World Cup ‌qualifiers. The match between top-ranked Spain and the Olympic champions was billed as a marquee showdown but the visitors took control as Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro scored inside 15 minutes. Spain's AdrianaNanclares saved a second-half penalty from Lily ​Yohannes to keep a clean sheet for the world ⁠champions. "When you play the best team ⁠in the world you have to execute everything really well in the first instance," said Hayes.

news.title: OPINION: Will Kenya ever play in the FIFA World Cup?
news.lede: Every four years, millions of Kenyans passionately follow the FIFA World Cup. We wear the jerseys of Argentina, Brazil, France, England, Germany, Spain or Morocco. We celebrate goals, debate tactics and dream that perhaps one day Kenya will also be part of football's greatest stage.
